exposure: Mode of delivery (caesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
outcome: Contraceptive method choice (highly effective, moderately effective, least effective)
cohort: The study sample included 4277 women aged 15-49 years who had a live birth in the 2 years preceding the 2021 survey in Nigeria.
finding: Caesarean delivery was independently associated with higher overall postpartum contraceptive use.
mod_finding: Compared with women who had vaginal deliveries, those who had caesarean sections had significantly higher odds of overall postpartum contraceptive use (aOR = 1.52; 95% CI 1.03 to 2.25).
cross-section timing: Data was analyzed from the 2021 Nigeria Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey, focusing on women who had a live birth in the 2 years preceding the survey.
